channel.title: RoofPayback blog
channel.description: Daily articles on U.S. electricity prices and rooftop solar payback, built on EIA and PVWatts data.

item.title: Fixed Charges on Your Electric Bill: Why Using Less Saves Less
item.description: Real 2026 fixed charges from California, Georgia Power and FPL, what each adds to the price of a kWh, and how a fixed charge stretches solar payback.

item.title: Are Solar Panels Worth It in 2026? A State-by-State Answer
item.description: No federal credit, lower export credits in some states: where solar still pays back in under 10 years, where it takes 16 or more, and what help is left.

item.title: Electricity Prices in September 2026: Winners and Losers
item.description: U.S. home electricity averaged 18.17¢/kWh in September 2026, up just 0.7%, the smallest gain in a year. The 12-month view and every big state mover.

item.title: How Electricity Prices Changed in Ten Years, by State
item.description: Residential electricity rose 41% nationally from 2016 to 2026 (12.9¢ to 18.2¢/kWh). See where prices doubled and where they barely moved.

item.title: Which States Use the Most Electricity per Home?
item.description: Louisiana homes average 1,231 kWh a month versus 507 in California. See usage, bills and prices for the highest and lowest states, and why use isn't cost.

item.title: Solar Quote Checklist: What to Verify Before You Sign
item.description: Three numbers to check on any solar quote, a worked example that exposes an optimistic payback, and the contract terms to confirm before you sign.

item.title: How Much Electricity Does a Solar Panel Make Monthly?
item.description: Month-by-month output per kW of solar panels for all 50 states and D.C., from PVWatts, plus how to scale it to one panel or a whole system.

item.title: Is Solar Worth It in New York? The Payback Math
item.description: New York's 25% state solar credit (up to $5,000) cuts our example payback from 9.1 to 7.4 years with full export credit. The math for typical and upstate homes.

item.title: Is Solar Worth It Where Electricity Is Cheap?
item.description: In the six states under 14¢ per kWh, solar takes 15 to 18 years at $3.50 a watt. See the price per watt that gets it to 12 years, and what daytime use adds.

item.title: Solar in Alaska vs. Hawaii: Which Pays Back Faster?
item.description: Hawaii still wins, but new systems no longer get retail credit. Payback with Hawaiian Electric's export rates, real household use and Alaska's range.

item.title: Solar Panels in the South Central States: TX, OK, AR, LA
item.description: Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas and Louisiana compared with September 2026 prices, and how a smaller system recovers payback when exports earn avoided cost.

item.title: Solar Panels on the Pacific Coast: Three States Compared
item.description: California, Oregon and Washington compared with each state's real household use, September 2026 prices and the crediting rules new solar customers face.

item.title: Solar Panels in the Mid-Atlantic: Payback by State
item.description: New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland and D.C. compared: solar payback, typical home use and nine-year price trends, with September 2026 data.

item.title: Is Solar Worth It in the Midwest? State-by-State Payback
item.description: Twelve Midwest states compared with September 2026 EIA prices: solar payback, typical home use, slow price growth out west and how Minnesota pays for surplus solar.

item.title: Solar Payback in the Southeast: Sun Meets Cheap Power
item.description: Ten Southeastern states compared with September 2026 prices: solar payback, large typical homes, the Carolinas price split and Kentucky's export credit rule.

item.title: Why Is Electricity So Expensive in Hawaii? EIA Data
item.description: Hawaii homes paid 48.31¢ per kWh in September 2026, 2.7 times the U.S. average. Ten years of EIA data show when the gap widened and what it costs.

item.title: Can You Choose Your Electricity Supplier? States With Retail Choice
item.description: Some states let you pick your electricity supplier. Learn how retail choice works and how to compare a supplier's price per kWh with the EIA state average.

item.title: Solar Panels in the Mountain West: Payback by State
item.description: Eight Mountain states compared: solar payback with September 2026 prices, why right-sizing matters in the sunny south, and what monthly credits cost Idaho.

item.title: Solar Panels in New England: Prices, Sun and Payback
item.description: The six New England states compared: payback, typical home use, price trends and how Connecticut, Maine and Vermont credit solar exports (September 2026 data).

item.title: Is Solar Worth It in Texas? Buyback Rates and Payback
item.description: Texas has no statewide net metering, so your plan's buyback rate decides payback. See payback at buyback rates from 0 to 15.91¢ and in eight cities.

item.title: Is Solar Worth It in California in 2026?
item.description: Under California's Net Billing Tariff, our example home pays back in about 12 years, not 7. See the math, the right size for a typical home and what to ask.

item.title: Is Solar Worth It in Cloudy States? What the Numbers Show
item.description: What a solar kWh costs over 25 years in the eight lowest-sunshine states, compared with the grid price there, and how export credit changes the payback.

item.title: Solar Panels for an Electric Car: How Much Bigger?
item.description: How many kWh an EV adds, how much bigger the solar system gets, and why charging at night or at midday changes payback when exports earn less than retail.

item.title: Solar Panel Degradation: 0.5% vs 0.8% Over 25 Years
item.description: How much output panels lose over 25 years, where the 0.5% a year figure comes from, and what a faster rate does to payback and savings in six states.

item.title: Solar Payback If Electricity Prices Keep Rising
item.description: How flat, 2.5% and 4% yearly price growth change solar payback, and what each state's own price trend since 2016 would mean if it continued.

item.title: Daytime Power Use and Solar Payback: 30%, 40%, 60%
item.description: How using more power while the sun is up changes solar payback under full, half and quarter export credit, with results for Texas, Arizona, Maine and Louisiana.

item.title: Solar Loan vs. Cash: How Financing Changes Payback
item.description: Loan-financed solar cost $4.50 a watt against $3.00 for cash in 2025. See monthly payments, total interest and 25-year results in three states.

item.title: Solar Price per Watt by State: What Pays Back in 10 or 15 Years
item.description: The most you can pay per watt for a 10- or 15-year solar payback in every state, Berkeley Lab's 2025 price benchmarks, and when waiting for cheaper panels pays.

item.title: How to Lower Your Electric Bill: Find the Cause, Then Cut
item.description: Diagnose a high electric bill with EIA monthly data, then see what a saved kWh and a heat pump water heater are worth in every state at September 2026 prices.

item.title: Can a Solar System Be Too Big? Annual True-Up Explained
item.description: Past a year of your use, extra panels make kWh nobody pays for. See uncredited kWh and payback by size in four states, and what real true-up rules do.
